questionText:
Instruction execution in a processor is divided into $5$ stages, Instruction Fetch (IF), Instruction Decode (ID), Operand Fetch (OF), Execute (EX), and Write Back (WB). These stages take $5$, $4$, $20$, $10$, and $3$ nanoseconds (ns) respectively. A pipelined implementation of the processor requires buffering between each pair of consecutive stages with a delay of $2\text{ ns}$. Two pipelined implementations of the processor are contemplated:

(i) a naive pipeline implementation (NP) with $5$ stages and
(ii) an efficient pipeline (EP) where the OF stage is divided into stages OF1 and OF2 with execution times of $12\text{ ns}$ and $8\text{ ns}$ respectively.

The speedup (correct to two decimal places) achieved by EP over NP in executing $20$ independent instructions with no hazards is ________.
explanation:
Step 1: Naive Pipeline (NP) Analysis
Stage delays: $\text{IF} = 5\text{ ns}$, $\text{ID} = 4\text{ ns}$, $\text{OF} = 20\text{ ns}$, $\text{EX} = 10\text{ ns}$, $\text{WB} = 3\text{ ns}$.
Buffer delay = $2\text{ ns}$.
Clock cycle time ($T_{NP}$) = $\max(5, 4, 20, 10, 3) + 2 = 20 + 2 = 22\text{ ns}$.
Number of stages ($k_1$) = $5$.
Time taken to execute $N = 20$ instructions:
$T_{\text{total, NP}} = (k_1 + N - 1) \times T_{NP} = (5 + 20 - 1) \times 22 = 24 \times 22 = 528\text{ ns}$.

Step 2: Efficient Pipeline (EP) Analysis
The OF stage is divided into $\text{OF1} = 12\text{ ns}$ and $\text{OF2} = 8\text{ ns}$.
Stage delays: $5, 4, 12, 8, 10, 3\text{ ns}$.
Clock cycle time ($T_{EP}$) = $\max(5, 4, 12, 8, 10, 3) + 2 = 12 + 2 = 14\text{ ns}$.
Number of stages ($k_2$) = $6$.
Time taken to execute $N = 20$ instructions:
$T_{\text{total, EP}} = (k_2 + N - 1) \times T_{EP} = (6 + 20 - 1) \times 14 = 25 \times 14 = 350\text{ ns}$.

Step 3: Speedup Calculation
$\text{Speedup} = \frac{T_{\text{total, NP}}}{T_{\text{total, EP}}} = \frac{528}{350} \approx 1.50857 \approx 1.51$.
